1.visual: An alarm clock with a round face, two bells on top, and diagonal strike lines on the lower left and right sides indicating vibration or ringing. The clock face shows a short hour hand pointing to roughly 10 and a longer minute hand pointing to 12.
1.usage: Setting an alarm or reminder, wake-up or sleep schedule features, notification alert settings, countdown timer triggers.

2.visual: A calendar page with two rounded binding tabs at the top and a large empty content area below a horizontal divider line. The body of the calendar is blank with no date numbers or markings.
2.usage: Opening a date picker, navigating to a calendar view, scheduling an event, date input fields.

3.visual: A calendar page with two rounded binding tabs at the top and a checkmark centered in the lower content area. The checkmark indicates a confirmed or completed date.
3.usage: Marking a date as confirmed or booked, confirming an appointment, completed scheduled event, RSVP accepted status.

4.visual: A calendar page with two rounded binding tabs at the top, with a small analog clock icon overlaid in the lower-right corner of the calendar body. The clock shows hands positioned at approximately 10:10.
4.usage: Scheduling an event with a specific time, datetime picker input, viewing a timed appointment, calendar event with a time component.

5.visual: A calendar page with two rounded binding tabs at the top and six evenly spaced dots arranged in a 2x3 grid in the lower content area, suggesting multiple days or dates.
5.usage: Viewing a monthly or multi-day calendar overview, selecting a date range, browsing available dates, recurring event scheduling.

6.visual: A calendar page with two rounded binding tabs at the top and a plus sign positioned in the lower-right corner of the calendar body, indicating an add action.
6.usage: Creating a new calendar event, adding a date to a schedule, booking a new appointment, adding a task to a specific date.

7.visual: A calendar page with two rounded binding tabs at the top and two short horizontal lines with rounded ends centered in the lower content area, resembling a simplified text or list entry.
7.usage: Viewing event details on a date, a scheduled note or memo, calendar entry with a description, agenda or itinerary item.

8.visual: A calendar page with two rounded binding tabs at the top and an X mark centered in the lower content area, indicating cancellation or removal.
8.usage: Cancelling an event or appointment, removing a date from a schedule, declined calendar invite, deleting a booking.

9.visual: A plain circle with a clock face showing two hands: a short hour hand pointing roughly toward 10 and a longer minute hand pointing toward 12. No decorative elements or bells — a minimal clock.
9.usage: Displaying current time, time input fields, viewing hours of operation, timestamps on content.

10.visual: A circular clock face with an arrow curving counterclockwise around the outside of the circle from the right side, with the clock hands visible inside. The counterclockwise arrow wraps from the bottom-right back toward the left.
10.usage: Undoing a recent action with a time context, restoring a previous version, viewing history or recent activity, reverting to an earlier state.

11.visual: An hourglass shape with a wide top and bottom connected by a narrow pinched center, drawn with straight geometric lines. The silhouette resembles a figure-8 rotated, with no sand fill visible.
11.usage: Indicating a loading or waiting state, showing elapsed time or a countdown, time limit warnings, patience or pending status.

12.visual: A stopwatch with a circular body, a flat button on top (for start/stop), and a short diagonal line inside the face angled to the lower-left, representing a moving second hand or elapsed time marker.
12.usage: Timing a task or activity, performance benchmarks, countdown or elapsed time display, sports or workout tracking.
